learningObjectives.title: Decision-making tools (decision trees, force-field, critical path analysis)

questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, strengths and weaknesses are:
questions.explain: Strengths/weaknesses are internal to the business; opportunities/threats are external.

questions.q: STEEPLE analysis examines the external environment, including social, technological, economic, environmental, political, legal and:
questions.explain: STEEPLE = Social, Technological, Economic, Environmental, Political, Legal, Ethical.

questions.q: Opportunities in a SWOT analysis are:
options: External factors the business could exploit
questions.explain: Opportunities are favourable external conditions; threats are unfavourable external ones.

questions.q: A new data-protection law affecting a business would appear under which STEEPLE factor(s)?
questions.explain: Legislation is a legal/political external factor in STEEPLE analysis.

questions.q: The Ansoff matrix's four strategies are market penetration, market development, product development and:
questions.explain: Ansoff: penetration, market development, product development and diversification.

questions.q: Diversification is considered the riskiest Ansoff strategy because it involves:
options: Both a new product and a new market
An existing product in an existing market
questions.explain: Diversification combines new products and new markets, so risk is highest.

questions.q: Selling an existing product to a new geographical market is:
questions.explain: Existing product + new market = market development in the Ansoff matrix.

questions.q: In the Boston (BCG) matrix, a 'cash cow' has:
options: High market share in a low-growth market
Low share in a high-growth market
High share in a high-growth market
Low share in a low-growth market
questions.explain: Cash cows generate steady cash with high share in mature (low-growth) markets.

questions.q: A decision tree evaluates options using:
questions.explain: Decision trees calculate expected values from estimated probabilities and payoffs.

questions.q: The expected value of an outcome is calculated as:
questions.explain: Expected value = payoff × probability, summed across outcomes.

questions.q: Force-field analysis (Lewin) weighs:
options: Driving forces for change against restraining forces
questions.explain: Force-field analysis compares forces pushing for and resisting a change.

questions.q: In critical path analysis (CPA), the critical path is:
options: The sequence of activities that determines the minimum project duration
questions.explain: The critical path has zero float; delaying any activity on it delays the whole project.

questions.q: 'Float' (slack) in critical path analysis is:
options: Spare time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project
questions.explain: Float is the amount of delay possible on a non-critical activity without extending the project.

questions.q: A decision tree gives Option A an expected value of £60,000 and Option B £45,000 (similar risk). On expected value alone, a manager should choose:
questions.explain: With similar risk, the higher expected value (Option A) is preferred, though qualitative factors also matter.

questions.q: Porter's generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and:
questions.explain: Porter identified cost leadership, differentiation and focus (niche) strategies.

questions.q: A cost-leadership strategy means competing by:
options: Being the lowest-cost producer in the industry
Only serving a niche at premium prices
questions.explain: Cost leadership seeks competitive advantage through the lowest costs.

questions.q: A circular business model aims to:
options: Design out waste by reusing and recycling resources
questions.explain: Circular models keep resources in use, contrasting with the linear take-make-dispose model.

questions.q: Strategic decisions differ from tactical decisions in that strategic decisions are:
options: Long-term and made by senior management
questions.explain: Strategic decisions are long-term and high-level; tactical decisions are shorter-term and operational.

questions.q: A limitation of SWOT analysis is that it:
options: Can be subjective and does not itself provide solutions
questions.explain: SWOT organises factors but is subjective and does not, by itself, decide strategy.

questions.q: A key limitation of decision trees is that they:
options: Rely on estimated probabilities that may be inaccurate
questions.explain: Decision-tree results are only as reliable as the estimated probabilities and payoffs used.
